resources.string: Needs one verified manual run on this build first.
Qualified on this build. Not enabled.
Enabled: one attempt per full boot, never after a soft reboot.
EARLY_JOB_NOT_ARMED. After arming, start one FULL reboot within 10 seconds.

This arms ONE early root attempt for the next full boot. The chain runs inside the boot animation, before BOOT_COMPLETED.

Confirming REBOOTS THE PHONE IMMEDIATELY. That is deliberate: the arming is only valid for %1$d seconds, and reaching the system reboot menu by hand often takes longer than that on a device that has just slowed down again.

A hard reboot is the recovery boundary if the chain fails.
Also arm the Early Boot Probe (observation only)
Soft reboot automatically in the same boot

Runs right after root completes, at whatever moment that falls — you may see one brief restart, sometimes over the boot animation and sometimes just after the lock screen appears. Landing it inside the animation was measured and is not reachable on this firmware. It is still gated: it needs this boot\'s verified root, the pinned daemon and the firmware\'s own boot-health verdict, and it refuses rather than forcing. One attempt per boot.
Leave the screen off and try again in about %1$d minutes. The reading above is the fact; the estimate comes from one observation of this device cooling ~3 °C per minute with the screen off.
The arming was rolled back, so nothing is pending and the next reboot will not run the chain.\n\nThe automatic reboot was refused by the platform:
This build returned an arming line it cannot account for, so it is reporting NOT ARMED rather than guessing. Nothing was scheduled that this app can confirm. The full line is in the log below.

EARLY_ROOT_NOT_ARMED. Arms ONE early root attempt for the next full boot: the chain runs inside the boot animation, before BOOT_COMPLETED. Needs a verified manual run on this build. A hard reboot is the recovery boundary.
The outcome of a DirtyFrag run, including unattended ones at boot.

KernelSU is re-running the module lifecycle. This app cannot observe the result directly: the restart tears down the process that would have watched it. A boot-health record was written before the handover and the restarted framework completes it, so the outcome can be read afterwards instead of guessed.

The root shell outlived its deadline, so whether KernelSU received the request is unknown. Root is unaffected. A full reboot re-applies modules through post-fs-data; this action will not run again in this boot.
